Two Kinds of Many-to-Many

TicketTag is a plain link between two tables; TicketWatcher is a link that carries its own data — and that difference has to show up in the schema.

Tickets and tags are M:N — you'd model this in Laravel with a plain pivot table and belongsToMany(). Prisma actually offers a shorthand for exactly that case, but this project deliberately models both of its M:N relationships as explicit join models instead, because one of the two needs to carry data the shorthand has no room for. Figure 2.8 is the plain case.

// Figure 2.8: a plain join table (prisma/schema.prisma, excerpt)
model TicketTag {
  ticketId Int
  tagId    Int

  ticket Ticket @relation(fields: [ticketId], references: [id])
  tag    Tag    @relation(fields: [tagId], references: [id])

  @@id([ticketId, tagId])
}

@@id([ticketId, tagId]) is a composite primary key — the pair of columns together is unique, not either column alone (the same one ticket can have several tags; the same tag can be on several tickets — just never the exact same pairing twice). Beyond that, TicketTag carries no information of its own — it only ever answers "is this tag on this ticket?"

Figure 2.9 looks almost identical, but isn't.

// Figure 2.9: a join table with its own data (prisma/schema.prisma, excerpt)
model TicketWatcher {
  ticketId        Int
  userId          Int
  notifyOnComment Boolean @default(true)

  ticket Ticket @relation(fields: [ticketId], references: [id])
  user   User   @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])

  @@id([ticketId, userId])
}

notifyOnComment is a genuine extra column on the relationship itself — whether this particular watcher wants comment notifications, not a property of the ticket or the user alone. That's precisely why Prisma's implicit-M:N shorthand (and Eloquent's plain belongsToMany()) wouldn't fit here: both assume a join table with nothing but the two foreign keys. The moment the relationship needs its own attribute, it has to become a real model you can add fields to — which is exactly what TicketTag and TicketWatcher now demonstrate side by side, from the same schema file.
